title: Initial launch and user bootstrap
description:
Goal
- On first app load, ensure a backend user and session exist and persist identifiers in an app cookie for subsequent visits.

Flow (finalized)
- On app startup, BootstrapGate initializes the OpenAPI client and ensures a token exists in a non-blocking effect. It always renders children and never performs navigation.
- Token resolution order: server-provided token (HttpOnly cookie via server), otherwise read client cookie safely; if missing, call backend bootstrap to create/init user + session; then set token on the generated OpenAPI client.
- Errors do not block rendering. A small, dismissible banner with a Retry button is shown. Retry re-attempts bootstrap.
- Routing to Chat is handled by the Root page ('/' -> '/chat') and not by BootstrapGate. This prevents double-navigate races.

Tech notes
- Use the generated axios/OpenAPI client in src/generated/backend. Configure base URL and token in a small wrapper (src/lib/api/init-openapi.ts) via env vars, and set the token with setAccessToken(token) after bootstrap.
- Cookie strategy: prefer HttpOnly cookie when feasible (server-side), with client cookie fallback only for minimal token propagation needed by the OpenAPI client. Client cookie parsing is hardened to never throw on malformed third‑party cookies.
- Bootstrap is performed in a React effect to avoid render‑time side effects and hook order mismatches. BootstrapGate never calls router.replace.
- UserProvider reads initial uid/token in a safe, try/catch wrapped initializer so render never throws.
- An app-level ErrorBoundary wraps the entire client tree; chat surfaces inline banners/toasts for retryable errors.

Acceptance criteria
- First visit without cookie performs backend bootstrap, persists identifiers, sets token in the OpenAPI client, and app renders Chat (via Root page redirect) without blocking UI.
- Subsequent visits reuse the cookie/token and do not recreate the user; no redundant bootstrap calls are made.
- Errors surface a non-blocking banner with Retry and do not crash or prevent page reloads.
- No in-render navigation is performed by bootstrap logic; navigation is handled only by pages/routes.

features.title: OpenAPI configuration bootstrap
features.description: Create a small startup initializer that sets the OpenAPI client base URL and token. Implementation: in 'src/lib/api/init-openapi.ts', export 'initOpenAPI(baseUrl: string)' and 'setAccessToken(token: string | undefined)'. Usage: import { OpenAPI } from '@/generated/backend/core/OpenAPI'; within init, set 'OpenAPI.BASE = baseUrl' (from process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL at app startup) and 'OpenAPI.TOKEN = token' when available after auth. All service calls will directly import from '@/generated/backend' without an extra wrapper.

features.title: App cookie schema and storage
features.description: Define cookie keys and shape for user identification (e.g., 'cw_uid', 'cw_session' or opaque token if backend supplies one). Prefer HttpOnly cookie set via backend or Next.js route handler; fallback to non-HttpOnly only if necessary. Document expiry (e.g., 180 days) and scope ('/'). Acceptance: cookie is written on first successful bootstrap and read on subsequent visits to hydrate user context.

features.title: Bootstrap endpoint integration
features.description: On missing app cookie, call backend bootstrap/login endpoint using the generated client. Example: 'import { AuthService } from '@/generated/backend'' and 'await AuthService.authControllerLogin({ body })' (or the specific bootstrap endpoint). Persist returned identifiers (userId, access token) and set 'OpenAPI.TOKEN'. Acceptance: first-visit flow creates user/session, sets cookie, and prepares OpenAPI for subsequent calls.

features.title: Startup bootstrap hook and guard
features.description:
Implement client-side bootstrap in a non-blocking effect within BootstrapGate:
- Initialize OpenAPI base URL from NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL.
- Resolve token in this order: server-provided prop from HttpOnly cookie, else safe client cookie read (never throws), else call backend bootstrap to create/init user + session.
- Set the token on the generated OpenAPI client via setAccessToken(token).
- Never navigate or block rendering from BootstrapGate; always render children. Root page handles '/' -> '/chat'.
- On error, show a small retryable banner/toast; allow reattempts without redirects.

Acceptance:
- First visit without cookie bootstraps and sets token while UI remains interactive; redirect to '/chat' is handled only by the Root page.
- Subsequent visits reuse the existing token and avoid redundant bootstrap calls.
- Errors are non-blocking, retryable, and do not crash reloads.

features.title: Error handling and retry UX
features.description: Provide a small banner/toast with retry for bootstrap failures. On error, keep the user on a safe route (e.g., '/'), allow retrying the bootstrap call, and log errors to console for MVP diagnostics. Acceptance: simulated 4xx/5xx shows retry; successful retry proceeds to Chat.

features.title: Client-side user state provider and hydration
features.description:
Introduce a lightweight global user state for immediate client access.
- Create a UserProvider (React Context) with state: { uid: string | null; tokenAvailable: boolean; profile?: Partial<UserProfileModel>; hydrated: boolean } and a 'useUser' hook.
- Hydrate from bootstrap cookies on mount (uid, token presence); optionally support a later 'me' fetch to enrich profile.
- Keep storage in-memory (no localStorage) for now; ensure safe SSR/CSR boundaries.
Acceptance criteria:
- After bootstrap, client components can synchronously read 'uid' and 'tokenAvailable' without re-fetching.
- State is consistent across navigations; errors in optional profile fetch are non-blocking.
